name: Treasury Fiscal Data
description: US Treasury Fiscal Data: the national debt to the penny, daily cash balances and tax receipts, monthly receipts and outlays, Treasury auction results, interest rates and expense on the debt, the gold reserve and official exchange rates.

tools.name: Auction results
tools.description: How an auction went: filter `security_type:eq:Note,security_term:eq:10-Year` and sort `-auction_date` for the last ten-year, then read `high_yield` and `bid_to_cover_ratio`. Bidder takedown comes as amounts, not shares: `indirect_bidder_accepted`, `direct_bidder_accepted` and `primary_dealer_accepted` in dollars, beside the `_tendered` amounts; an indirect share is `indirect_bidder_accepted` divided by `total_accepted`. `cusip:eq:` reaches one security. Bills report discount rates, notes and bonds yields, TIPS real yields, FRNs discount margins.

response.about: Records at `data`, oldest first unless sorted. Every value is a string, amounts included, and a missing value is the string `null` rather than JSON null. `meta` beside it carries `count`, `total-count`, `total-pages`, and a `labels`, `dataTypes` and `dataFormats` map for the returned columns; `links` carries the paging query strings. One row per auctioned security since November 1979, keyed by CUSIP and auction date: the terms, the high, low and median rates or yields, bid-to-cover, and the amounts tendered and accepted by competitive, non-competitive, direct, indirect, primary-dealer, SOMA and FIMA bidders. A column that does not apply to the security type - a discount rate on a note, a coupon on a bill - is `null`. Amounts, `offering_amt` included, are whole dollars, not millions. 114 columns, and none of the `src_line_nbr` or fiscal-period columns the other datasets end with.

tools.name: Operating cash balance
tools.description: The Treasury General Account balance - the government's cash on hand - which is what debt-ceiling coverage tracks day by day. For the current figure filter `account_type:eq:Treasury General Account (TGA) Closing Balance`, sort `-record_date` and read `open_today_bal`; `close_today_bal` is `null` on every row since 2022-04-18. The same balance is `close_today_bal` on `account_type:eq:Federal Reserve Account` rows through 2021-09-30 and on `account_type:eq:Treasury General Account (TGA)` rows for the six months between, so a series across the 2022 relabelling is those three filters stitched together.

Every value is a string, amounts included, and a missing value is the string `null` rather than JSON null. `meta` beside it carries `count`, `total-count`, `total-pages`, and a `labels`, `dataTypes` and `dataFormats` map for the returned columns; `links` carries the paging query strings. Table I of the Daily Treasury Statement: one row per account type per business day since October 2005, in millions of dollars. The account labels follow the statement's own layout, which changed twice. Through 2021-09-30 the cash balance is the `Federal Reserve Account` row and from 2021-10-01 to 2022-04-15 the `Treasury General Account (TGA)` row, each with the day's close in `close_today_bal` and the opening balances for the day, month and fiscal year alongside; the Tax and Loan Note, Supplementary Financing Program and Short-Term Cash Investment accounts are rows of their own over that period. From 2022-04-18 the table is four TGA rows - `Treasury General Account (TGA) Opening Balance`, `Total TGA Deposits (Table II)`, `Total TGA Withdrawals (Table II) (-)` and `Treasury General Account (TGA) Closing Balance` - on which `close_today_bal` is `null` and the day's figure sits in `open_today_bal`, with `open_month_bal` and `open_fiscal_year_bal` carrying the month and fiscal-year figures of the same line (on the closing-balance row all three repeat the day's close).

response.about: Records at `data`, oldest first unless sorted. Every value is a string, amounts included, and a missing value is the string `null` rather than JSON null. `meta` beside it carries `count`, `total-count`, `total-pages`, and a `labels`, `dataTypes` and `dataFormats` map for the returned columns; `links` carries the paging query strings. Table 1 of the Monthly Treasury Statement since March 2015, one row per line of the table per statement month: gross receipts, gross outlays and the deficit (positive) or surplus (negative), in dollars. Each `record_date` carries two fiscal-year sections, the prior year printed first and the current year second. `classification_desc` names the line: `FY 2026` on a section heading (`sequence_level_nbr` 1, amounts `null`), a month name - `October` through `September` - on a month row (`record_type_cd` `MTH`), and `Year-to-Date` on the section's running total. A month name therefore appears twice per record date, once per section; the current fiscal year's row is the one with the higher `line_code_nbr` (160 to 280, against 20 to 140 for the prior year), or equivalently the one whose `parent_id` is the `classification_id` of the current `FY` heading. Line codes are strings, so `gte` on them compares text, not numbers.

tools.name: Treasury reporting rates of exchange
tools.description: The official rate a US agency reports a foreign balance at, per quarter. Filter `country_currency_desc:eq:Euro Zone-Euro` or `country:eq:Japan`, add `effective_date:lte:<date>` for the date being reported, and sort `-record_date,-effective_date`, so the first row is the rate in force on that date rather than an amendment that came after it. For a market rate on a given day this is the wrong source.

Every value is a string, amounts included, and a missing value is the string `null` rather than JSON null. `meta` beside it carries `count`, `total-count`, `total-pages`, and a `labels`, `dataTypes` and `dataFormats` map for the returned columns; `links` carries the paging query strings. The rate, in units of foreign currency per US dollar, that federal agencies use to convert foreign-currency balances for reporting, per country and currency per quarter-end since March 2001. A quarter-end is not always one row: when a rate is amended mid-quarter the amendment is a further row with the same `record_date`, country and currency and a later `effective_date` - Bolivia at 2026-06-30 carries 6.85 effective 2026-06-30 and 10.35 effective 2026-07-15. A caller wanting one value per quarter takes the row whose `effective_date` is the latest on or before the date in question: filter `effective_date:lte:<date>` first, then sort `-effective_date` so that row comes first. Sorting alone picks the latest amendment, which for a date before it took effect is the wrong rate. Not a market rate and not daily.
